propositions: The Pass-2/Pass-3 judge exhibits unacceptable self-consistency drift across repeated runs on the same input, measured over 50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort; Fleiss' kappa must be ≥0.6 AND raw agreement ≥0.8 for R5's new sub-answer to be stable.

Section-order permutation of plan input causes the gate verdict to flip between PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE across 3 distinct reorderings; order-sensitivity must be below the κ≥0.6 AND raw-agreement≥0.8 floor (Fleiss' kappa + exact-agreement on verdict) before R3 adds order-exposed container criteria.

Infra-level INDETERMINATE verdicts (carrying llm_unavailable or verify_failed coverage flags) represent execution failures, not stable judge outcomes, and must be excluded from agreement metrics and re-run until 3 substantive votes/verdicts are collected or explicitly capped and reported.

The judge's existing Pass-2 binary sub-answers and the deterministic Pass-3 decision path (decision ∈ {block, advisory, dropped, indeterminate}) provide the unit of agreement for self-consistency; Pass-3 is deterministic given Pass-2, so all measured variance is Pass-2 stochasticity.
